This notebook is designed to analyze environmental data collected from a warehouse. The analysis will include data cleaning, visualization, and statistical modeling to understand the environmental conditions within the warehouse.

# Experiment Configuration
```{r}
# -------------
# DEFINE EXPERIMENT NAME
# ---------------

experiment_name <- "Penetration_Test"

```
This should match the name of the data file (without the .xlsx extension) in the Data folder. For example, if the data file is named "Experiment.xlsx", then experiment_name should be set to "Experiment".

## Set Folder Directory 
```{r}
input_folder <-
  "C:/Users/Daniel Jackson/Desktop/R/Warehouse Environments Analysis/Data"

processed_folder <-
  "C:/Users/Daniel Jackson/Desktop/R/Warehouse Environments Analysis/Processed_Data"

```

## Set Room Dimensions
```{r}
# Coordinate system:
#
# Origin = back-left-floor
#
# X = Width
# X increases from left -> right
#
# Y = Length
# Y increases from back -> front
#
# Z = Height
# Z increases from floor -> ceiling

room_width_ft  <- 25 # ft

room_length_ft <- 35 # ft

room_height_ft <- 30 # ft

room <- list(
  width = room_width_ft,
  length = room_length_ft,
  height = room_height_ft
)

room
```

## Door Configuration
```{r}
# Door wall:
#
# "back"
# "front"
# "left"
# "right"


door_wall <- "front"


door_width_ft <- 12

door_height_ft <- 14


# Position of CENTER of door
#
# Back/front wall:
#   position is X / Width
#
# Left/right wall:
#   position is Y / Length


door_center_ft <-
  room_width_ft - 8   #This sets the center of the door to 8 ft from the total room length. Adjust as needed. 
```

## Spatial Resolution for Interpolation
```{r}
grid_resolution_x <- 2 #ft 

grid_resolution_y <- 2 #ft 

grid_resolution_z <- 2 #ft 

# This sets the spatial resolution for the interpolation grid. Adjust as needed for finer or coarser resolution.
```

## IDW Interpolation Power Parameter
```{r}
idw_power <- 2
```

## Create the room boundaries
```{r}
# ============================================================
# CREATE ROOM BOUNDARIES
# ============================================================

corners <- data.frame(

  X = c(
    0,
    room_width_ft,
    room_width_ft,
    0,
    0,
    room_width_ft,
    room_width_ft,
    0
  ),

  Y = c(
    0,
    0,
    room_length_ft,
    room_length_ft,
    0,
    0,
    room_length_ft,
    room_length_ft
  ),

  Z = c(
    0,
    0,
    0,
    0,
    room_height_ft,
    room_height_ft,
    room_height_ft,
    room_height_ft
  )

)

corners$ID <- c(
  "A",
  "B",
  "C",
  "D",
  "E",
  "F",
  "G",
  "H"
)

corners
```
The corners are:

          E -------- F
         /|         /|
        / |        / |
       G -------- H  |
       |  |       |  |
       |  A ------|--B
       | /        | /
       |/         |/
       C -------- D

Where:

A = bottom-back-left
B = bottom-back-right
C = bottom-front-right
D = bottom-front-left
E = top-back-left
F = top-back-right
G = top-front-right
H = top-front-left


Create the 12 edges
```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------
# Define the 12 edges
# --------------------------------------------------

edge_pairs <- data.frame(

  from = c(
    "A", "B", "C", "D",
    "E", "F", "G", "H",
    "A", "B", "C", "D"
  ),

  to = c(
    "B", "C", "D", "A",
    "F", "G", "H", "E",
    "E", "F", "G", "H"
  )

)

edge_pairs
```

### Convert the edges into Plotly coordinates
```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------
# Build plotting data for the room edges
# --------------------------------------------------

room_edges <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    1:nrow(edge_pairs),
    function(i) {

      start <- corners[
        corners$ID == edge_pairs$from[i],
      ]

      end <- corners[
        corners$ID == edge_pairs$to[i],
      ]

      data.frame(
        X = c(start$X, end$X, NA),
        Y = c(start$Y, end$Y, NA),
        Z = c(start$Z, end$Z, NA)
      )
    }
  )
)

rownames(room_edges) <- NULL

head(room_edges, 15)
```

## Add a Temperature_C column to the data frame
```{r}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    Temperature_C =
      (Temperature_F - 32) * 5 / 9
  )
```


## Calculate dew point
```{r}
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    gamma =
      log(Relative_Humidity_pct / 100) +
      (
        17.625 * Temperature_C
      ) /
      (
        243.04 + Temperature_C
      ),

    Dew_Point_C =
      243.04 * gamma /
      (
        17.625 - gamma
      )

  )
```

## Calculate dew point depression
```{r}
data <- data %>%

  mutate(

    Dew_Point_F =
      Dew_Point_C * 9 / 5 + 32,

    Dew_Point_Depression_F =
      Temperature_F - Dew_Point_F

  ) %>%

  select(
    -gamma
  )
```

```{r}
names(data)
```
# Interpolation

## Create a grid for interpolation
```{r}
interpolation_grid <- expand.grid(

  X_ft = seq(
    0,
    room_width_ft,
    by = grid_resolution_x
  ),

  Y_ft = seq(
    0,
    room_length_ft,
    by = grid_resolution_y
  ),

  Z_ft = seq(
    0,
    room_height_ft,
    by = grid_resolution_z
  )

)

nrow(interpolation_grid)
```
## IDW Interpolation Function
```{r}
# ============================================================
# IDW INTERPOLATION FUNCTION
# ============================================================

interpolate_variable <- function(
    sensor_data,
    grid,
    variable,
    idp = idp
) {

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Keep complete observations for this variable
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  sensor_data <- sensor_data %>%

    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[variable]]),
      !is.na(X_ft),
      !is.na(Y_ft),
      !is.na(Z_ft)
    )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Convert sensor locations to SpatialPointsDataFrame
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  coordinates(sensor_data) <-
    ~X_ft + Y_ft + Z_ft


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Convert interpolation grid to SpatialPoints
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  coordinates(grid) <-
    ~X_ft + Y_ft + Z_ft


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # IDW interpolation
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  result <- gstat::idw(

    formula =
      as.formula(
        paste(
          variable,
          "~ 1"
        )
      ),

    locations = sensor_data,

    newdata = grid,

    idp = idp

  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Return ordinary data frame
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  result <- as.data.frame(result)


  # Rename predicted value
  names(result)[
    names(result) == "var1.pred"
  ] <- paste0(
    "Predicted_",
    variable
  )


  # Keep only required fields
  result %>%

    select(
      X_ft,
      Y_ft,
      Z_ft,
      starts_with("Predicted_")
    )

}
```

      "Y_ft",

  left_join(

    by = c(

      "Y_ft",

    )

    by = c(
      "X_ft",
      "Y_ft",
      "Z_ft"
    )

## Create a function to interpolate all four variables for a given timestamp
```{r}
# ============================================================
# INTERPOLATE ONE TIMEPOINT
# ============================================================

interpolate_timepoint <- function(

    timestamp,
    data,
    grid,
    idp = 2

) {

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Sensor observations for this timestamp
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  sensor_data <- data %>%

    filter(
      Timestamp == timestamp
    )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Interpolate temperature
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  temperature <- interpolate_variable(

    sensor_data,
    grid,
    "Temperature_F",
    idp

  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Interpolate relative humidity
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  humidity <- interpolate_variable(

    sensor_data,
    grid,
    "Relative_Humidity_pct",
    idp

  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Interpolate dew point
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  dew_point <- interpolate_variable(

    sensor_data,
    grid,
    "Dew_Point_F",
    idp

  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Interpolate dew point depression
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  dpd <- interpolate_variable(

    sensor_data,
    grid,
    "Dew_Point_Depression_F",
    idp

  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Combine the four interpolated fields
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  result <- temperature %>%

    left_join(
      humidity,
      by = c(
        "X_ft",
        "Y_ft",
        "Z_ft"
      )
    ) %>%

    left_join(
      dew_point,
      by = c(
        "X_ft",
        "Y_ft",
        "Z_ft"
      )
    ) %>%

    left_join(
      dpd,
      by = c(
        "X_ft",
        "Y_ft",
        "Z_ft"
      )
    ) %>%

    mutate(
      Timestamp = timestamp
    )


  result
}
```

processed_environmental_fields_final <-
  processed_environmental_fields %>%

  mutate(

    Experiment_ID = experiment_name,

    Grid_Resolution_X_ft = grid_resolution_x,

    Grid_Resolution_Y_ft = grid_resolution_y,

    Grid_Resolution_Z_ft = grid_resolution_z,

    IDW_Power = idw_power

  ) %>%

  select(

    Experiment_ID,

    Timestamp,

    X_ft,
    Y_ft,
    Z_ft,

    Predicted_Temperature_F,

    Predicted_Relative_Humidity_pct,

    Predicted_Dew_Point_F,

    Predicted_Dew_Point_Depression_F,

    Grid_Resolution_X_ft,
    Grid_Resolution_Y_ft,
    Grid_Resolution_Z_ft,

    IDW_Power

  )
